function: Predicts RIS phase shifts, BS transmit and receive beamformers, and UL and DL transmit powers to maximize the weighted sum rate in full-duplex transmission (p. 1, 4).
system: Full-duplex BS, ULA with Mt=10 transmit and Mr=10 receive antennas; two passive reflecting RISs, 36 elements each; single-antenna users; 3.5 GHz, 100 MHz (p. 3, 9-10).
method: Two stages: least-squares self-interference cancellation, then DDPG deep reinforcement learning with feature extractor and sub-networks; online, reward-driven; quantized and grouped-phase variants (p. 4-8).
data_channel: Simulated Rician LOS (K 9 and 6 dB) plus Rayleigh NLOS with Jakes' method at 100 Hz Doppler; path loss from a white paper; no dataset (p. 9).
test_conditions: Agent trained online and evaluated in the same simulated environment; separate runs for static and moving users, BS antenna counts, 2-3 bit phases, grouping, one-RIS model (p. 9-13).
baselines: Non-learned: random RIS phases and beamformers (RandPSBF). Learned: DRL of [32], perfect-CSI and noisy-CSI DRL, OU-noise variant of proposed DRL (p. 9-10, 12).
metrics: UL and DL data rates in bits/s/Hz as learning curves and CDFs; signaling bits from BS to RIS; FLOP counts (p. 9, 11-13).
complexity: FLOPs per network given in closed form; Table II lists 2.9e4 (PerfCSI-DRL), 3.3e4 (MSF-DRL), 5.46e4 (MSF(Q)-DRL, grouped variant) (p. 13).
q1_support: p. 9: "time-dependent Rayleigh fading using the Jakes" method for the NLOS part plus Rician LOS, with path loss from a 5G white paper (ref. [56], p. 15): a custom simulator, not TR 38.901 or measured data.
q2_support: p. 9: "experiment is run for an initial 100 episode"; p. 11: "the trained DRL agents are used to get the rate distribution" in the same environment. Each scenario is learned anew; no trained agent is tested in another one.
q3_support: p. 9: RandPSBF "tries to randomly predict the RIS phases and beamformers" (non-learned); p. 12: "method with [32] in Fig. 8", an earlier DRL method for RIS-assisted full duplex, compared on UL and DL rates.
q4_support: p. 13: "the total number of floating point operations (FLOPs) at the feature extractor" is derived, and Table II lists the FLOPs of the proposed methods.
q5_support: p. 9: "time-dependent Rayleigh fading using the Jakes" shows a self-built simulated channel; the paper gives no code or data link, no public dataset and no measurements.
notes: Title and DOI on p. 1 match. Area 3 because the DDPG agent outputs RIS phases, beamformers and powers; the first stage is a least-squares estimate, not learned. q3 rests on RandPSBF and [32]. q1 is not met because small-scale fading is Rician/Rayleigh and only the path loss cites a 5G white paper. Table II was read from the page image.
